guide.summary: Internal or personal use only (self-serve, wait none); Public app, sensitive or restricted scopes (app review, wait 3-5 business days for sensitive scope verification); Public app, non-sensitive scopes only (approval path unconfirmed). Where the path is unconfirmed, the agent did not find it in the provider's docs.
guide.verdict: Easiest: Internal or personal use only (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app, sensitive or restricted scopes (app review, wait 3-5 business days for sensitive scope verification).

composio.note: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Gmail (OAUTH2). It shows Composio's name to users and shares quota across all Composio users.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype: Composio's managed Gmail app works. For production you usually want your own app so users see your name, you control scopes, and you get a dedicated quota.
reasons: Consent screen shows your app name instead of Composio
Composio's default scopes may not cover what you need
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Enterprise customers may require end-to-end branding
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval

prerequisites.title: Google Cloud project with consent screen
prerequisites.detail: You need a Cloud project with Branding, Audience and Data Access configured, including app name, support email and contact email.

prerequisites.title: Public home page and privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: The home page must be publicly accessible, and the privacy policy must be hosted on the same domain and linked from the consent screen.

prerequisites.title: Verified domain ownership
prerequisites.detail: Authorized domains must be verified in Google Search Console by an Owner or Editor of the project.

steps.title: Decide audience and scopes
steps.detail: Choose internal vs public and the narrowest Gmail scopes; check each scope's sensitivity in the Google API docs.
steps.done_when: You know which scopes you need and whether they are sensitive or restricted.

steps.title: Draft scope justifications
steps.detail: Draft why each sensitive scope is needed and why a narrower scope is not enough, plus a demo video script.
steps.done_when: Justification text and video script are ready for review.

steps.title: Create Cloud project and consent screen
steps.detail: Log in to Google Cloud, enable billing if publishing on the Marketplace, and fill in Branding, Audience and Data Access.
steps.done_when: Consent screen is saved with the right user type and scopes.

steps.title: Create OAuth client and Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create an OAuth client in Google Cloud. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into it, then create the Composio auth config with your client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: Composio auth config for gmail uses your own credentials.

steps.title: Publish branding and verify domain
steps.detail: Verify domain in Search Console, publish branding, and run brand verification from the Branding page.
inputs: Home page and privacy policy URLs

steps.title: Record demo video
steps.detail: Record in English the OAuth grant flow, consent screen with app name and client ID in address bar, and each sensitive scope's feature. Upload as Unlisted on YouTube.

steps.title: Submit for verification
steps.detail: Submit via the OAuth Verification Center with justifications and the video link.
steps.done_when: Data access status shows in review.

steps.title: Wait for Google verification
steps.detail: Google's Trust & Safety team may email for more information; respond promptly.

steps.title: Test with a real connected account
steps.detail: Connect a test user through Composio and confirm your app name appears on the consent screen.
steps.done_when: Gmail tool calls succeed for the test account.

traps.title: Leaving the app in Testing
traps.detail: Testing apps allow only 100 listed test users and limit refresh tokens to 7 days.

traps.title: Unverified app caps users
traps.detail: A published unverified app with sensitive or restricted scopes shows danger warnings and is capped at 100 total users.

traps.title: Branding is locked during verification
traps.detail: Branding changes are not allowed while verification is in progress; you must cancel it first. Brand verification results expire after 7 days if unpublished.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio's name
traps.detail: Users see 'Composio wants to access your account' with the managed app, and quota is shared.

traps.title: Request the narrowest scopes
traps.detail: Many scopes overlap, so choosing a non-sensitive scope can avoid extra reviews.

traps.title: Marketplace audience cannot be changed
traps.detail: Only relevant if you also list on the Workspace Marketplace: public or private cannot be changed after publishing.

blockers.symptom: Error 403: rate_limit_exceeded on the consent screen
blockers.what_it_means: The app is gaining new users faster than its new-user authorization rate limit allows.
blockers.what_to_do: Check the grant rate on the OAuth consent screen page and request a quota increase.

blockers.what_it_means: The app has not completed verification.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the consent screen configuration and prepare the submission text.

blockers.symptom: A customer's Workspace admin blocks the app
blockers.what_it_means: Admins can block any OAuth app, even verified ones.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer's admin to mark your client ID as Trusted or add it to their allowlist.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft admin instructions with your client ID.

open_questions: Is the Gmail scope https://mail.google.com/ (and read/send scopes) sensitive or restricted? Check the scope sensitivity in the Gmail API scopes reference and the Cloud Console sensitive indicator.
Does a restricted Gmail scope require a security assessment, and how long does it take? Check the Google restricted-scope verification docs.
What is the exact total user cap for unverified apps with sensitive scopes beyond the 100 stated? Check the Unverified apps page.
Will Gmail API overage charges apply to your usage after Google's 2026 billing change? Check the Gmail API quota page for the billing details.

evidence.quote: Generally, you should choose the most narrowly focused scope possible and avoid requesting scopes that your app doesn't require.
evidence.answer: Developers should choose the most narrowly focused scope possible and avoid requesting scopes the app does not require.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: For any scopes listed in the "Your sensitive scopes" or "Your restricted scopes" sections, try to identify alternative non-sensitive scopes to avoid unnecessary additional reviews.
evidence.answer: For sensitive or restricted scopes, the developer should look for non-sensitive alternatives to avoid extra reviews.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Users more readily grant access to limited, clearly described scopes.
evidence.answer: Users are more willing to grant access when scopes are limited and clearly described.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: If you selected External for user type, add test users:
evidence.answer: For apps with External user type, the developer must add test users; the page gives no maximum number of test users.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: For some workarounds users might be shown the "unverified app" screen.
evidence.answer: For some workarounds, users might be shown an "unverified app" screen.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: OAuth verification is required for sensitive or restricted scopes. You can still save your app as a draft, but you're not able to publish your draft app listing.
evidence.answer: With unverified sensitive or restricted scopes, the draft listing cannot be published until verification is done.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: If you update your app to use different scopes that are sensitive or restrictive, you must submit your app for OAuth verification again.
evidence.answer: Changing the app to use different sensitive or restricted scopes requires submitting for OAuth verification again.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: You don't need to send it for app review again.
evidence.answer: A scope change that requires re-verification does not require sending the app through app review again.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Before publishing your app, ensure billing is enabled in your Google Cloud project, the app is built and tested, you understand authentication & authorization concepts, and your Google Cloud project is updated for Apps Script projects (if applicable).
evidence.answer: The developer must have billing enabled in the Google Cloud project before publishing; the page gives no API fees or pricing.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: When your app is installed, a user is asked to validate the scopes used by the app.
evidence.answer: When the app is installed, the user is asked to validate the scopes the app uses.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Scopes added to the Google Workspace Marketplace SDK are used for domain-wide and individual installs to authorize your app when it's installed from the Google Workspace Marketplace.
evidence.answer: Scopes added in the Marketplace SDK authorize the app for domain-wide and individual installs made from the Google Workspace Marketplace.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Under App Information , in App name , enter an App name .
evidence.answer: In the consent screen, the developer enters an app name under App Information.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: In User support email , choose a support email address where users can contact you if they have questions about their consent.
evidence.answer: The developer chooses a User support email on the consent screen where users can ask questions about consent.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Under Audience , select the user type for your app.
evidence.answer: The developer selects the user type for the app under Audience.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Under Contact Information , enter an Email address where you can be notified about any changes to your project.
evidence.answer: The developer enters a contact email under Contact Information to be notified about project changes.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: If you're creating an app for use outside of your Google Workspace organization, click Data Access > Add or Remove Scopes
evidence.answer: For apps used outside the developer's Google Workspace organization, scopes are added under Data Access > Add or Remove Scopes.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: After selecting the scopes required by your app, click Save .
evidence.answer: After choosing the scopes, the developer clicks Save.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: After you associate your Apps Script project with the Cloud project, your OAuth 2.0 credential is automatically created.
evidence.answer: For apps built in Apps Script, associating the Apps Script project with a standard Cloud project automatically creates the OAuth 2.0 credential.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: To create your OAuth 2.0 credential, see OAuth client ID credentials
evidence.answer: For apps not built in Apps Script, the OAuth 2.0 credential is created by following the OAuth client ID credentials guide.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: When publishing your app, you must complete four main tasks related to authentication and authorization: fill out the OAuth consent screen, create your OAuth 2.0 credential, configure all necessary scopes, and submit your app for OAuth verification (if applicable).
evidence.answer: Publishing involves filling out the consent screen, creating an OAuth 2.0 credential, configuring scopes, and submitting for verification where applicable.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Scopes define the level of access your app has to user data and must be configured in the OAuth consent screen, Google Workspace Marketplace SDK, and the manifest (if applicable).
evidence.answer: Scopes must be configured in the OAuth consent screen, the Marketplace SDK, and the manifest (if applicable).

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Enter the required information, and click Submit for verification
evidence.answer: To submit for verification, the developer enters the required information and clicks Submit for verification.
